chunks: As for whatever is in it from Al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays, I have narrated it from my father—may Allah have mercy on him—from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Mismaʿī, from al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays.
And he was a mawla of al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, a Kufan, a cloth seller, and Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī killed him.

key_terms.الْمُعَلَّى بْنِ خُنَيْسٍ: Al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays, the transmitter being identified here
key_terms.بَزَّازٌ: A cloth merchant or seller of fabrics
key_terms.قَتَلَهُ دَاوُدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: A note that he was killed by Dāwūd ibn ʿAlī
key_terms.كُوفِيٌّ: A native or resident of Kufah
key_terms.مَوْلَى الصَّادِقِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: A client or freed servant associated with Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage gives the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits reports from al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays. It also briefly identifies al-Muʿallā ibn Khunays as a mawla of Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, from Kufah, and notes his profession and death.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Everything in this book that is narrated from Al-Mualla ibn Khunays has been transmitted by me from my father - may Allah (swt) have mercy on him - from Sad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Masmai, from Al-Mualla ibn Khunays.
He was a freed servant (mawla) of Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), a Kufan, and a cloth seller (bazzaz). He was killed by Dawud ibn 'Ali.
